title: 5 risk rules that keep trading accounts alive
caption: Strategy gets the attention. Risk keeps the account. The 5 rules that decide who's still trading in a year. Save this.

slides.title: Never more than 1%
slides.body: Risk 1% of the account per trade — 2% absolute max. At 1%, a 10-loss streak costs ~10%. At 5%, it ends you. The number isn't conservative. It's survival math.

slides.title: Hard daily loss limit
slides.body: Down 3% on the day → laptop closed. No exceptions, no 'just one more'. Most blown accounts die in a single revenge session, not over months.

slides.title: Size off the stop, not the gut
slides.body: Position size = risk amount ÷ stop distance. The chart decides your size. Never 'feel' bigger because you're confident. Confidence is not edge.

slides.title: One-directional de-risking
slides.body: After a loss streak you drop to half size. You only return to full size after sustained recovery — not one good trade. Easy to get defensive, hard to get aggressive again.

slides.title: Journal every loss
slides.body: Every loss: was the rule followed, yes or no. 'Followed the rule and lost' is fine. 'Broke the rule' — even on a win — is the actual problem. Track that, not P&L.

slides.quote: Amateurs think about how much they can make. Professionals think about how much they can lose.

slides.sub: The rules + the journal template. Free.
